Q Nguyen

A Vietnamese Restaurant That Actually Gets It Right
Jan 2026 • Family
Namme has cracked the code that most Vietnamese restaurants miss: how to honor tradition while pushing the cuisine forward. Dishes arrive familiar enough to satisfy traditionalists, yet inventive enough to feel contemporary without being gimmicky.

What really sets them apart is that portions are intentionally small, which is brilliant. You can order multiple dishes and actually taste the full range of what the kitchen is doing. It's like a tasting menu with the freedom to choose your own path.

The villa setting is amazing, offering a rare open space that doesn't feel cramped, a luxury for Saigon. The atmosphere alone makes the experience feel special.

What impresses me most is that this restaurant doesn't play favorites with its audience. Traditional Vietnamese diners eat with genuine satisfaction, while friends with Western palates are equally enthusiastic. The food doesn't pander to either side.

The French Tire Manufacturer has been recommending Vietnamese places for years, but many don't touch what Namme is doing here. It's skilled, thoughtful cooking that respects where Vietnamese cuisine comes from while imagining where it can go.

The only downside is that it's a little off the beaten path, away from where most tourists congregate. But it's still worth the short trip.

If you've been disappointed by the plateau most Vietnamese restaurants settle into, Namme is worth a visit.
